description: Berkelium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Bk and atomic number 97, a member of the actinide and transuranium element series. It was discovered in December 1949 at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in Berkeley, California, making it the fifth transuranium element discovered.
uses: Berkelium has no practical application outside scientific research, which is mostly directed at the synthesis of heavier transuranium elements and superheavy elements. For example, a sample of berkelium-249 was used to synthesize the new element tennessine for the first time in 2009.
characteristics: Berkelium is a soft, silvery-white, radioactive metal with a density of 14.78 g/cm³ and a melting point of 986 °C. The berkelium-249 isotope emits low-energy beta particles and decays with a half-life of 330 days to californium-249. It exhibits paramagnetic behavior between 70 K and room temperature with an effective magnetic moment of 9.69 Bohr magnetons, and undergoes a transition to an antiferromagnetic state upon cooling to about 34 K.
